codeReview.summary: The fix correctly addresses the blocking issue from the milestone-scrutiny review. The timeout handler in spawnScrutinyProcess now calls proc.kill?.('SIGTERM') immediately after setting killed=true, preventing orphaned child processes. The ProcLike interface was updated with an optional kill method. A new test verifies that kill('SIGTERM') is called on timeout using a custom mock spawn that tracks kill calls. The fix is minimal, targeted, and follows the established pattern from spawn-worker.ts's setup command timeout handler. All 2296 tests pass, typecheck clean, lint clean.

issues.description: No SIGKILL fallback after SIGTERM. spawn-worker.ts's killProc helper has a setTimeout that sends SIGKILL if the process hasn't died after SIGTERM. However, spawn-worker.ts's own setup command timeout handler (line 557) also uses bare SIGTERM without fallback, so this is consistent with existing patterns. The scrutiny process is a pi subprocess that should respond to SIGTERM; a hung process ignoring SIGTERM is an edge case not worth the added complexity here.

summary: Fix adequately addresses the blocking issue from the milestone-scrutiny review. The original issue was that the timeout handler in spawnScrutinyProcess set killed=true but never called proc.kill(), leaving orphaned pi reviewer processes. The fix adds proc.kill?.('SIGTERM') to the timeout handler, adds kill as an optional method on ProcLike, updates MockChildProcess with a kill method, and adds a test verifying kill is called with 'SIGTERM' on timeout. The implementation is clean, minimal, and follows established patterns. Pass.
